hypotheses.justification: If P ≠ 0, this follows from the case assumption; if P = 0, Nat.Coprime P M₁ forces M₁ = 1. In that case choose g₁ = g: mapN 0 is the identity and mapN 1 is trivial. Thus a proof can split on P = 0 and use the existing CRT proof otherwise.

If M₁ ≠ 0, this follows from the case assumption; if M₁ = 0, Nat.Coprime P M₁ forces P = 1. In that case choose g₁ = 1: mapN 1 is trivial and mapN 0 sends 1 to 1. Thus a proof can split on M₁ = 0 and use the existing CRT proof otherwise.
